entities.name: IceCube
entities.does: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos
notable: Found the first high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, 2013
Traced one 2017 event back to a flaring blazar
Mapped neutrino emission from the plane of our own galaxy, 2023

entities.name: ICEYE
entities.does: Small radar satellites that image through cloud and darkness
notable: Put the first smallsat synthetic-aperture radar in orbit

The API most consumer AI products are built on

entities.name: Rocket Lab
entities.does: Electron small launcher
notable: Electron reached orbit in 2018 and is the busiest small launcher
Launched CAPSTONE to lunar orbit for NASA in 2022
Recovers boosters from the sea to study reuse
Neutron, a larger reusable vehicle, is in development

entities.name: SpaceX
entities.does: Falcon 9 and Starship launch vehicles
notable: Falcon 9: first orbital-class booster landing in 2015, now routine and reflown
Dragon: first commercial crew flight, Demo-2, in 2020
Starship: full flight tests since 2023, booster caught by the tower in 2024
Starlink: by far the largest satellite constellation ever operated
Launched Europa Clipper for NASA in October 2024

entities.name: ActInSpace
entities.status: every two years — 2026 finals in Bordeaux
entities.does: A 24-hour contest to turn a real space patent into a business idea

entities.name: AI Security Institute
entities.does: State-run evaluations of frontier models for dangerous capabilities

entities.name: AI2
entities.does: Fully open models — weights

entities.name: ALPHA

entities.name: AMS-02

entities.name: Arc Institute
entities.org: non-profit, with Stanford, UCSF and Berkeley
entities.does: Where AI and biology meet as one lab: genome language models built next to the wet benches that test them.
notable: Its Evo models read and write DNA across all domains of life
Used a genome language model to design working bacteriophages
Funds scientists for years at a time, not grant cycles

entities.name: Astroscale
entities.does: Rendezvous with and removal of dead satellites and debris — the orbital cleanup business
notable: ELSA-d demonstrated magnetic capture of a client satellite in 2021
ADRAS-J flew right up to a discarded Japanese rocket stage in 2024 and photographed it
Working toward actually removing debris, not just approaching it

entities.name: ATLAS
entities.does: General-purpose proton collisions — Higgs properties and searches for new particles
notable: Co-discovered the Higgs boson in 2012
Has published thousands of measurements and searches since
Being rebuilt now for the High-Luminosity LHC

entities.name: BioNTech
entities.does: Founded to make cancer immunotherapy, became famous for a vaccine, and has gone back to cancer.
notable: Co-developed the first authorised mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, with Pfizer
Founders Uğur Şahin and Özlem Türeci started it for cancer, not viruses
Oncology pipeline now includes bispecific antibodies

entities.name: Blue Origin
entities.does: New Shepard suborbital flights and New Glenn
notable: New Shepard has flown crew on suborbital hops since 2021
New Glenn reached orbit on its first flight, January 2025
Building the Blue Moon lunar lander for NASA's Artemis programme

entities.name: Broad Institute
entities.full_name: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
entities.does: Genomics at industrial scale, and the lab behind base editing and prime editing.
notable: Base and prime editing now in more than 25 clinical trials
gnomAD has contributed to over 13 million genetic diagnoses
Has sequenced nearly 900,000 whole human genomes

entities.name: Caltech SURF
entities.status: annual — proposals due in the winter
entities.does: A summer of research at Caltech or JPL, written up and defended like a real project — students propose the work themselves.
notable: Running since 1979
Students write their own proposal with a mentor
JPL projects are part of the same programme

entities.name: CERN Summer Student

entities.does: Eight to thirteen weeks on a real project at CERN, with a lecture series alongside it. Paid: a net allowance of 94 CHF per day, health insurance, and travel costs in some cases.

entities.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
entities.does: A compact tokamak made possible by high-temperature superconducting magnets — the magnets are the whole bet.
notable: SPARC is designed to be the first commercially relevant machine to produce net fusion energy
ARC, the power plant meant to follow it, is already sited
The largest private fusion company by funding

entities.name: Copernicus Masters
entities.does: Prizes

entities.name: CRISPR Therapeutics
entities.does: Makes the first approved CRISPR medicine: patients' own stem cells, edited and returned.
notable: Casgevy, developed with Vertex, is approved for sickle cell disease and beta thalassaemia
Co-founded by Emmanuelle Charpentier
The first time gene editing became a prescription

entities.name: DESY Summer Students
entities.does: Seven and a half weeks inside a major accelerator laboratory, on photon science, accelerators, particle or astroparticle physics.
notable: 2026 edition ran 21 July to 10 September
Free hostel accommodation plus a daily stipend, travel partly reimbursed

entities.name: EleutherAI
entities.does: Grassroots open-source research collective; released open models when almost nobody else did

entities.name: ESA Business Incubation

Mars gravity assist, March 2025

entities.name: Exotrail
entities.does: Electric thrusters and an orbital transfer vehicle — the tow truck that moves satellites
notable: spacevan, an orbital transfer vehicle, has flown
ExoMG Hall thrusters fly on other operators' smallsats
Sells the manoeuvre, not the hardware — mobility as a service

entities.name: FASER

entities.name: Fervo Energy
entities.does: Geothermal power anywhere hot rock is deep enough, using the horizontal drilling and fibre sensing the oil industry perfected.

Building Cape Station in Utah
Staffed deliberately with oil and gas engineers

entities.name: Firefly Aerospace
entities.does: Alpha launch vehicle and the Blue Ghost lunar lander

Alpha is its small launch vehicle
One of the few commercial landers to reach the Moon intact

entities.name: Google DeepMind
entities.does: Gemini
notable: AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in 2016

entities.name: Google Summer of Code

notable: Over 21,000 contributors since 2005, across 1,000+ organisations
Astropy, the HEP software projects and similar groups participate regularly
Contact the organisation before the proposal window — that is what decides selection

entities.name: Helion
entities.does: Pulsed magneto-inertial fusion that aims to turn the plasma's energy straight into electricity, skipping the steam turbine.
notable: Polaris: the first privately built machine to show measurable deuterium-tritium fusion

Building Orion, which it calls the first fusion power plant

entities.name: Hubble
entities.does: Optical and ultraviolet astronomy — still the sharpest UV eye we have
notable: The Deep Field (1995): point at nothing, find thousands of galaxies
Pinned down the expansion rate, and started the tension over its value
Still working after 35 years and five servicing missions

entities.name: Hugging Face

entities.name: ImageSat International

entities.name: Intuitive Machines

IM-2 Athena followed in March 2025
Flies under NASA's commercial lunar payload programme

entities.name: ISS
entities.does: Continuously crewed laboratory — microgravity science and the testbed for everything that follows

AMS-02 has been mounted outside since 2011
The testbed for every commercial crew and station programme that follows

entities.name: JUICE

Venus flyby 2025; Jupiter arrival planned 2031

entities.name: KATRIN

entities.name: LHCb

entities.name: Meta FAIR

entities.name: Mila

entities.name: Mistral AI
entities.does: Europe's frontier lab

entities.name: Moderna

entities.name: NASA Space Apps Challenge
entities.does: A weekend hackathon on real agency data; local events run in Israel and across Europe

2.05 MJ of laser light produced 3.1 MJ of fusion yield
Ignition has since been repeated at higher gain

entities.org: private, spun out of Oxford University
entities.does: Perovskite layered on silicon — two cells in one, each catching the part of sunlight the other wastes.
notable: Built on Henry Snaith's perovskite research
Among the first to put perovskite-silicon tandems into commercial modules
Tandems are how solar gets past the single-junction efficiency limit

entities.name: Parker Solar Probe
entities.does: Flying through the Sun's corona to find out what heats it and accelerates the solar wind

Closest approach December 2024, about 6.1 million km from the surface
Fastest object ever built by humans

entities.name: Perseverance
entities.does: Roving an ancient river delta and caching samples for a future return mission

Sample tubes cached at Three Forks, waiting for a return mission
Found organic molecules in Jezero's delta rocks

entities.does: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays — where the most energetic particles in nature come from

entities.name: Planet Labs

SkySat adds high-resolution tasking on top of that baseline
Archive now spans more than a decade of daily coverage

entities.does: Israel's space education pipeline — school programmes

entities.name: Ramon.Space
entities.does: Radiation-tolerant computers for spacecraft — supercomputing that survives orbit
notable: Radiation-tolerant processors that keep working through orbital radiation
Aimed at moving real computation off the ground and into the spacecraft
Opened US engineering operations near Denver

entities.name: Rubin Observatory
entities.does: Will image the whole southern sky every few nights for ten years
notable: First-look images released June 2025
Will repeat the whole southern sky every few nights for ten years
Expected to multiply the number of known solar system objects

entities.name: SolarEdge
entities.does: The electronics between a solar panel and the grid — optimisers and inverters that get more out of every roof.
notable: Installed in more than 140 countries
Leads in rooftop solar capacity
Moved into home storage and grid services

entities.name: StemRad
entities.does: The AstroRad vest
notable: AstroRad flew on Artemis I around the Moon, on the MARE experiment
Also tested aboard the ISS
Shields bone marrow selectively rather than the whole body

entities.name: StoreDot
entities.does: Silicon-anode batteries built to charge an electric car in minutes rather than hours.
notable: Extreme-fast-charging cells at 300 Wh/kg
Partnerships with Mercedes, Volvo and Polestar
Backed by bp and TDK

entities.name: T2K
entities.does: Neutrino oscillation and hints of CP violation in the lepton sector

entities.name: TerraPower
entities.does: Natrium, a sodium-cooled fission reactor with molten-salt storage bolted on — so the plant can surge when the grid needs it.
notable: First plant under construction in Wyoming
345 MWe, with over five hours of molten-salt energy storage
Also developing medical isotopes for cancer treatment

entities.name: Voyager 1 and 2
entities.does: The only working instruments humanity has outside the Sun's bubble
notable: Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space in 2012, Voyager 2 in 2018
Engineers recovered Voyager 1 from a failed memory chip in 2024, from 24 billion km away
Instruments are being switched off one by one to stretch the power budget

entities.name: Weizmann Institute
entities.does: One of the world's leading basic-science institutes, strong in immunology, cancer and the gut microbiome.

entities.name: XRISM

canon.title: Achievement of Target Gain Larger than Unity in an Inertial Fusion Experiment
canon.why: 2.05 MJ of laser light in, 3.1 MJ of fusion out. Seventy years of trying, finally over the line.

canon.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
canon.why: A fifty-year-old problem, largely solved. The structures are free for every known protein.

canon.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
canon.why: GPT-3. The paper where scaling alone started producing abilities nobody trained for.

canon.title: Attention Is All You Need
canon.why: The transformer. Every large language model in use today is a descendant of this one paper.

canon.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger
canon.why: Spacetime itself was measured ringing, a century after Einstein said it would.

canon.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
canon.why: Skip connections made very deep networks trainable. Almost everything since is built on them.

canon.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
canon.why: Two networks trained against each other — the idea that made generated images convincing.

canon.title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson
canon.why: The last missing piece of the Standard Model, found 48 years after it was predicted.

canon.title: A Programmable Dual-RNA–Guided DNA Endonuclease in Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
canon.who: Jinek, Chylinski, Fonfara, Hauer, Doudna and Charpentier
canon.why: CRISPR-Cas9 turned from a bacterial immune system into a tool for editing any genome.

canon.title: Suppression of RNA Recognition by Toll-like Receptors
canon.why: The modified-nucleoside trick that stops the body attacking mRNA. Ignored for years, then it made the COVID vaccines work.

canon.title: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe
canon.why: The expansion is speeding up, and nobody knows why. Dark energy is the name for not knowing.

canon.title: Evidence for Oscillation of Atmospheric Neutrinos
canon.why: Neutrinos change type as they travel, which means they have mass — the Standard Model said they did not.

canon.title: LixCoO2: A new cathode material for batteries of high energy density
canon.why: The cathode inside the lithium-ion battery in your phone. A Nobel, 39 years later.

canon.title: The hippocampus as a spatial map
canon.why: The discovery of place cells — the brain's internal map. Nobel Prize 2014.

canon.title: Self-Consistent Equations Including Exchange and Correlation Effects
canon.why: The practical form of density functional theory — how most of computational chemistry works today.

canon.title: A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s
canon.why: They thought it was pigeon droppings in the antenna. It was the afterglow of the Big Bang.

canon.title: Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex
canon.why: How the visual cortex builds edges and shapes out of spots of light — and an inspiration for convolutional networks.

canon.title: Detailed Balance Limit of Efficiency of p-n Junction Solar Cells
canon.why: Why a single solar cell tops out near a third of the sunlight it catches — and why tandems exist.

canon.title: Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay
canon.why: Nature tells left from right. Physicists had assumed for decades that it could not.

canon.title: Synthesis of the Elements in Stars
canon.why: How every element heavier than helium got made. The paper that ties nuclear physics to the sky.

canon.title: Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor
canon.why: How hot, how dense and for how long — the bar every fusion machine is still measured against.

canon.title: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid
canon.why: One page, and the double helix. Built on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data, which she was not told they had.

canon.title: A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve
canon.why: The equations for how a neuron fires. Still the basis of every realistic neuron model.

canon.title: Über den Nachweis und das Verhalten der bei der Bestrahlung des Urans mittels Neutronen entstehenden Erdalkalimetalle
canon.why: The chemistry showing uranium had split into barium. They could not explain it, and published anyway.

canon.title: Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction
canon.why: The explanation Hahn could not give, worked out over a winter walk. Meitner was left off the Nobel.

canon.title: The Nature of the Chemical Bond
canon.why: Quantum mechanics turned into the chemist's everyday picture of bonds and hybrid orbitals.

canon.title: A relation between distance and radial velocity among extra-galactic nebulae
canon.why: Two and a half pages showing the universe is expanding. Cosmology starts here.

books.title: Bayesian Data Analysis
books.who: Gelman, Carlin, Stern, Dunson, Vehtari and Rubin
books.why: How to reason about uncertainty when you have a model and not much data. Free PDF from the authors.

books.title: Numerical Recipes
books.why: The algorithms behind the library functions you call, explained well enough to know when they will fail you.

books.title: Statistical Data Analysis
books.why: The standard reference for how physicists actually handle errors, fits and limits. Short, and nothing wasted.

books.title: Data Reduction and Error Analysis for the Physical Sciences
books.why: The first statistics book most physics students meet, and the one they keep going back to.

books.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
books.why: If you are going to publish plots, read this before you publish more of them.

books.title: An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics
books.why: The standard undergraduate course in one very heavy volume — stars, galaxies, cosmology, all of it.

books.title: Introduction to Cosmology
books.why: The clearest first cosmology book there is. You can read it end to end without getting stuck.

books.title: Black Holes and Time Warps

books.title: The First Three Minutes
books.why: A Nobel laureate walking through the early universe minute by minute, without hiding the physics.

books.title: Liftoff
books.why: How SpaceX nearly died before Falcon 1 reached orbit. Reported, not mythologised.

books.title: Reentry
books.why: The sequel: Falcon 9, reuse, and the decisions that turned a survivor into the whole market.

books.title: Space Mission Analysis and Design
books.why: The engineering reference the industry actually sizes missions with. Known simply as SMAD.

books.title: The Right Stuff
books.why: Why anyone climbs onto a rocket at all. Still the best writing about test pilots and nerve.

books.title: Modern Particle Physics
books.why: The current standard course. Works the calculations through instead of quoting results.

books.title: Introduction to Elementary Particles
books.why: Griffiths explains things the way a good supervisor would. Start here before Thomson.

books.title: Review of Particle Physics
books.why: Every measured property of every known particle, updated yearly and free. The field's single most-used document.

books.title: Lost in Math
books.why: An argument that beauty has been a bad guide in theoretical physics. Contested, and worth arguing with.

books.title: Plasma Physics and Fusion Energy
books.why: What it would actually take to build a fusion reactor, with the engineering constraints left in.

books.title: The Making of the Atomic Bomb
books.why: A Pulitzer for a book that is also a genuine history of 20th-century nuclear physics. Read it for Meitner and Bohr.

books.title: Midnight in Chernobyl
books.why: Reactor physics as it behaves when institutions fail. The clearest account of what actually happened.

books.title: Deep Learning
books.why: The foundations, from linear algebra up. Free online, and still the reference for why things work.

books.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
books.why: Bridges classical statistics and deep learning in one framework. Draft PDF free, code in Python and JAX.

books.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
books.why: By the people who built the field. Free PDF, and still the clearest treatment of the basics.

books.title: The Alignment Problem
books.why: The honest version of why making these systems do what we meant is hard, told through the research.

books.title: Sustainable Energy — Without the Hot Air
books.why: Every energy argument turned into kilowatt-hours per person per day. Free online, and it settles a lot of arguments.

books.title: Molecular Biology of the Cell
books.why: The textbook of cell biology. If you come from physics, this is where the vocabulary comes from.

books.title: The Gene
books.why: From Mendel to gene editing, written by an oncologist with a family history that makes it personal.

books.title: The Code Breaker
books.why: Jennifer Doudna and the race to CRISPR, with the rivalries left in.

books.title: The Emperor of All Maladies
books.why: A biography of cancer. Won the Pulitzer, and explains why the mRNA cancer vaccines matter so much.

items.title: Leading Axion Sensitivity with Interstellar Medium Optical Line Emission
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We introduce interstellar optical line emission as a new probe of axion dark matter. Axion decays to photons or electrons can excite or ionize neutral hydrogen, producing H$α$ emission at a fixed atomic wavelength rather than at an energy set by the axion mass. Developing the formalism and applying it to the Leo T galaxy with Very Large Telescope data, we derive strong constraints for eV--GeV scale axions, covering new regions of parameter space for both axion-photon and axion-electron couplings. These results establish optical line measurements as a new discovery channel for axion dark matter, probe poorly constrained parameter space below hydrogen's ionization threshold, and constrain axion explanations of JWST's high-redshift supermassive-black-hole observations.

items.title: NEXONN: Advancing the NEXOTRANS Exoplanet Atmospheric Retrieval Framework with Transformer-Based Neural Posterior Estimation for JWST Transmission Spectroscopy of WASP-39b
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope is delivering unprecedented constraints on exoplanet atmospheres, but computationally intensive Bayesian retrievals challenge the transition from individual planets to population-level studies of planetary formation and evolution. We introduce NEXONN, a transformer-conditioned normalizing-flow framework within NEXOTRANS that enables rapid atmospheric posterior estimation with uncertainty quantification. Incorporating PandExo-based JWST noise, we benchmark NEXONN against PyMultiNest using simulated spectra and JWST observations of WASP-39 b (0.6-12 microns). For simulated MIRI/LRS data, eight posteriors achieve a mean overlap of 80.32%. Retrievals of combined NIRISS, NIRSpec, and MIRI observations yield consistent atmospheric properties. For the full dataset, NEXONN infers C/O = 0.82 (+0.01/-0.02) and [M/H] = 1.13 (+0.04/-0.04), compared with PyMultiNest values of 0.80 (+0.03/-0.01) and 1.19 (+0.05/-0.03). Divergence metrics, Wasserstein distances, posterior overlaps, and coverage tests assess posterior fidelity and uncertainty calibration, revealing parameter-dependent differences. Once trained, NEXONN performs posterior inference within seconds, enabling scalable population studies of exoplanet atmospheric composition, formation, and evolution.

items.title: Isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux limits from Carpet-3 experiment data using neural networks with domain adaptation
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Diffuse gamma rays above 100 TeV probe PeV cosmic rays and astrophysical neutrino sources. Their strong attenuation on background radiation makes the observed flux sensitive to the location of the emission and to possible modifications of photon propagation. Searches for an isotropic component require rejection of an overwhelming hadronic background, but uncertainties in air-shower physics, cosmic-ray composition and detector response can lead to differences between simulated and measured events. Here we report upper limits on the isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux from 100 TeV to 10 PeV using 1078 days of Carpet-3 observations collected between 2022 and 2026. We identify photon candidates with a neural network combining the surface-array signals and measurements from the upgraded 410 $\mathrm{m^2}$ muon detector. Unsupervised domain adaptation uses unlabeled experimental events during training to mitigate the impact of simulation--data discrepancies on the classification. The limits are among the strongest available and provide benchmarks for tests of extended Galactic emission and modified photon propagation from extragalactic sources.

items.title: Multimessenger Exoplanets: Combining Infrared Excess and Astrometry with Gravitational-wave Detections of Double White Dwarf Exoplanets
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Multimessenger astrophysics provides a powerful framework for characterizing astrophysical systems through multiple, independent signals rather than relying solely on electromagnetic (EM) observations. While most prior multimessenger studies have focused on the properties of ultracompact objects, recent work has shown that gravitational waves (GWs) detectable with the upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) observatory can also be used to detect exoplanets orbiting stellar remnants. In particular, this includes circumbinary planets around tight double white dwarf (DWD) systems. This population is unique: no such planets are currently known around DWDs, and only a handful of circumbinary planets around main-sequence stars and planets orbiting white dwarfs (WDs) have been identified. Independent EM confirmation will be essential, especially for the first GW-detected exoplanets, to validate this method. While EM techniques are unlikely to efficiently survey large populations of DWDs, GW detection followed by targeted EM confirmation provides one pathway for identifying and characterizing these systems. Using a representative case, the known DWD ZTF J2243+5242 scaled to a fiducial distance of 150 pc, we compute the detectability of circumbinary exoplanets via LISA GW observations. We then demonstrate two complementary EM techniques--JWST infrared (IR) excess and Gaia or Habitable Worlds Observatory astrometry--that could independently confirm a GW-detected planet in this fiducial system. We present the first exploration of IR excess around DWDs as a viable exoplanet detection method, extending its established use for solitary WDs. Both EM techniques overlap with regions of parameter space where LISA is sensitive to DWD exoplanets, enabling robust confirmation and characterization.

items.title: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p -wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1–3 ). Achieving p -wave superconductivity 4 and its magnetic analogue 5 —characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p -wave spin-polarized Fermi surface—remains a grand challenge 6,7 . Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p -wave magnets 5,7–10 , spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p -wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p -wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves S y polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted S y exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p -wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p -wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics 10 , topological matter 7 , superconductivity 11 and beyond.

items.title: Unraveling QCD dynamics via charm-tagged jets with ALICE at the LHC
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The study of jet substructure provides tests of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and offers differential ways to study hadronization mechanisms. QCD predicts that jet radiation patterns depend on the mass and color charge of the initiating parton. Parton showers are sensitive to the different Casimir factors of quarks and gluons, and to the parton mass through the dead-cone effect. In this talk, we present three sets of $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jet measurements. First, we present the first measurement of the Energy-Energy Correlator (EEC) for $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jets. This observable reveals the detailed structure of QCD radiation from heavy quarks, allowing for a distinction between perturbative and non-perturbative effects in charm-quark showers. We then discuss measurements of the angular differences between three different axis definitions inside the jets. The three definitions offer different sensitivity to wide-angle soft radiation and systematically probe the radiation pattern from charm quarks. The final measurement regards jet angularities, which characterize the weighted angular distribution of the jet constituents. These powerful observables probe the parton shower, with sensitivity to parton-mass and Casimir-factor related effects that can be tuned by adjusting the importance of wide-angle radiation.

items.title: Carbon dioxide and amorphous water ices in the debris disk around β Pictoris
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The star β Pictoris is orbited by a dusty debris disk, within which planet formation is occurring. The outer disk is sufficiently far from the star that volatile molecules are expected to freeze into solid ices. We observed the β Pictoris disk in the near-infrared using the James Webb Space Telescope. The spectrum shows features due to amorphous water ice (<7% crystallinity) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) ice in both the 12 CO 2 and 13 CO 2 isotopologues. We infer that the CO 2 ice is intimately mixed with the water ice at a ratio of 1:10. This implies that the ices formed in cold conditions, likely in the interstellar medium. Frequent collisions within the debris disk are required to explain the observed uniform distribution of icy dust grains.

items.title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies 1–4 . Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases 2,5,6 . However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space 7–12 ), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

items.title: Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Cannibalism, the consumption of conspecifics, is widespread across the animal kingdom and can profoundly influence individual fitness and population dynamics 1,2 . Although the ecological and social conditions that favour cannibalism have been well documented 2 , the molecular signals that trigger cannibalistic attacks have remained poorly understood. Here we show that in Locusta migratoria , guaiacol, a volatile compound with augmented release after injury, attracts gregarious nymphs and induces cannibalistic behaviour. Guaiacol is detected by olfactory receptors LmOR36 and LmOR34, and disruption of either receptor abolishes attraction, thereby impairing induction of cannibalism. Guaiacol is synthesized by haemolymph symbiont Enterobacter hormaechei . Injury promotes bacterial congregation at the wound site, leading to elevated guaiacol production through a clustered set of vanillic acid decarboxylase genes; deletion of this gene cluster abolishes guaiacol production and its behavioural effects. Notably, guaiacol initially functions as a beneficial signal after injury. Guaiacol activates immune-related pathways in wounded locusts, enhancing pathogen resistance and increasing survival following minor injury. However, when guaiacol emission exceeds a threshold determined by injury severity, it functions as an external cue that attracts cannibals. Cannibalistic locusts exploit this immune-related odour to locate severely injured conspecifics, gaining both nutritional resources and immune system benefits. Together, our findings identify a microbial–chemical mechanism that links immune defence with cannibalistic behaviour and provide potential molecular targets for manipulation of cannibalism-dependent population dynamics.

items.title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a key technology for compact, analogue and energy-efficient optical information processing 1 . Yet, their practical implementation remains limited by the intrinsically weak optical nonlinearities of conventional materials, which demand high power and large device footprints to achieve substantial nonlinear responses 2 . Exciton–polaritons, hybrid light–matter excitations of semiconducting materials, offer a promising route to overcome these limitations by combining strong optical nonlinearities with the high speed and scalability typical of photonic platforms 3–5 . However, despite their potential, fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification have remained elusive. Here we demonstrate a fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings these functionalities together in a single-step-grown platform. We realize precise and scalable polariton circuits with integrated gratings that act as both couplers and reflectors, enabling in-plane Fabry–Pérot cavities. These structures support robust in-plane polariton lasing with coherent guided emission at a geometry-defined wavelength, optical amplification of propagating polaritons and nonlinear optical phase control exceeding π, all within the same on-chip architecture. Our results establish perovskite polariton circuits as a scalable platform for active and interferometric integrated photonics.

items.title: Scalar inelastic scattering of pseudo-Majorana dark matter through a radion portal
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We investigate a radion portal for pseudo-Majorana dark matter as an interpretation of the high-recoil event LZ230616. In contrast to the familiar pseudo-Dirac regime, the pseudo-Majorana structure allows a dominant scalar transition while suppressing elastic scattering. Endothermic kinematics remove low-energy recoils, while the nuclear response shapes the surviving high-recoil spectrum. Combining the accepted LZ event count with the Born-level thermal relic abundance yields a reference solution with $m_χ=1$ TeV, $δ=340$ keV, and $m_r=30$ GeV. This solution lies within the published LZ spin-independent $\mathcal{O}_1^s$ interval and remains compatible with existing OPAL and CMS constraints, while a simplified HL-LHC diphoton projection could probe it. Solar neutrino searches offer a complementary test. The benchmark's energetic-daughter proxy rates are comparable in magnitude to the rate scales reconstructed from IceCube's direct $b\bar{b}$ and $τ^+τ^-$ templates. An illustrative IceCube-Gen2 rescaling suggests future sensitivity, while a model-specific assessment requires the radion-cascade neutrino spectra and detector response.

items.title: First observation of the decay $D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{*+}γ$ and measurement of the branching-fraction ratio $\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{*+} γ]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{+} γ]$

items.abstract: We report the first observation of the radiative decay $D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{*+} γ$ with a significance greater than 10 standard deviations. The signal is found in $e^{+}e^{-} \to c\bar{c}$ production using data samples with integrated luminosities of 980 and 572~$\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ collected by the Belle and Belle~II detectors operating at the KEKB and SuperKEKB asymmetric-energy $e^{+}e^{-}$ colliders, respectively. This result helps discriminate between different theoretical models regarding the internal structure of the charm-strange meson $D_{s1}(2460)^{+}$.

items.title: Geoneutrinos (and reactor neutrinos) do not visibly decay
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Neutrinos that decay on their way to a detector arrive depleted, more so at low energies, where time dilation lengthens their lifetime the least. Geoneutrinos---electron antineutrinos from the radioactive decay of uranium and thorium inside the Earth---have energies of a few MeV and travel up to the diameter of the Earth. We use them to test neutrino decay for the first time. We compute the geoneutrino signal at Borexino, KamLAND, SNO+, and JUNO for visible decay, in which the daughter neutrinos are themselves detected, and compare it against their published data. We find no evidence of decay that holds across Earth models. Combining the four experiments, we limit the decay $ν_1 \to ν_3$ in the inverted mass ordering at 90% C.L.: $τ_1/m_1 > 3.7 \times 10^{-9}$ s eV$^{-1}$ when the radiogenic power of the Earth is left free and $τ_1/m_1 > 4.4 \times 10^{-9}$ to $1.6 \times 10^{-8}$ s eV$^{-1}$ when it is taken from Earth models. With an Earth model assumed, the geoneutrinos set the limit; with the power free, the antineutrinos from nuclear reactors that the same experiments detect count as much as the geoneutrinos. These are the first terrestrial limits on the visible decay of $ν_1$.

items.title: Probing agent overeagerness in realistic settings with continuation audits
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Frontier coding agents increasingly exhibit overeagerness, taking surprising, sometimes reckless actions beyond a user's mandate --- reported in recent system cards from frontier model developers. These cases are surfaced through internal deployment monitoring, which requires private traffic and is out of reach for open-weight models and independent evaluators. Automated alignment audits are the natural alternative, but capable models increasingly recognise the synthetic setup and adjust their behaviour. We introduce Continuation Audits, a pipeline that grounds the auditor on a prefix drawn from a real coding-agent transcript and directs it to continue the trajectory toward a seeded behaviour. Because the prefix is drawn from a real session, the auditor only needs to maintain a realistic setting rather than manufacturing it. We validate the method on SWE-Chat prefixes: on a paired subset of 90 audits a judge cannot reliably distinguish continuations from their source sessions (realism win rate 0.42 vs.\ 0.43), and across all 900 audits verbalized eval-awareness does not exceed the rate observed in the unaudited real sessions. Applying the pipeline to three recent models across three seeds, we find each model leads a different seed --- DeepSeek~V4~Pro on colleague-credentials misuse, GPT-5.6~Terra on file-permission bypasses, and Kimi~K3 on treating diagnostic questions as instructions. Kimi~K3 additionally continues to bypass file-permission protections after an explicit CLAUDE.md prohibition while the other two stop entirely, corroborating Moonshot's own report of excessive proactiveness.

items.title: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome outbreak linked to cruise ship travel in April–May 2026
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: In April 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. ANDV genome sequences were obtained for 10 of the 13 identified cases during a cross-country investigation established to share initial raw data for joint analysis with reciprocal quality control. The genomic data, symptom onsets, and plausible contact patterns strongly support a tightly linked outbreak cluster compatible with a single or very few zoonotic spillover events prior to embarkment followed by human-to-human transmission onboard. The outbreak represents the international displacement of a virus already known to be capable, under specific conditions, to transmit among humans, and does not suggest emergence of a unusual viral strain.

items.title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Innate immune systems of living organisms are essential for host defense. Central to these systems is the Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, an evolutionarily conserved module. From antiphage systems in prokaryotes to innate immune systems in plants, TIR domains have catalytic activity. However, TIR domains within animal innate immune receptors, such as Toll-like receptors (TLRs), have been considered as scaffolds for adaptor recruitment. We report that the TLR4 TIR domain possesses an allosterically activated nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) hydrolase (NADase) activity that operates in a single-turnover manner. Its product, adenosine diphosphate ribose, is not released but entrapped as a “molecular glue,” stabilizing a composite catalytic pocket with adaptor TIR domain–containing adaptor protein (TIRAP) to nucleate signalosome assembly. This “produce-and-trap” mechanism represents a signaling mode that integrates enzymatic activity with adaptor function to drive downstream signaling.

items.title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Resistance in standard conductors decreases with increasing cross-section. Yet, in low-dimensional superconductors and superfluids, residual resistance arises from topological fluctuations of the order parameter, manifesting as phase slips in one-dimensional (1D) and vortices in two-dimensional (2D) systems. How resistance and dissipation evolve as geometry interpolates between these regimes remains an open question. This evolution is masked in solid-state experiments by disorder, impurities and geometric imperfections 1–3 , and poses theoretical challenges due to competing dissipative processes and pronounced finite-size effects. Here, we use a defect-free unitary Fermi gas in a digitally programmable transport geometry to isolate geometric effects on superfluid dissipation and discover a paradox: in the crossover from one dimension to two dimensions, the resistance reaches a minimum. There, widening a channel increases its resistance. Narrower, quasi-1D channels show dissipation described by Langer–Ambegaokar–McCumber–Halperin theory of phase slips 4 . In this regime, varying the channel width yields the predicted exponential scaling of the activation factor over many orders of magnitude. Wider, quasi-2D channels show dissipation consistent with phase-slip events described by a finite-size vortex model 5 . The minimal dissipation in the dimensional crossover reflects a transition in the dominant dissipative mechanism, with both 1D and 2D events simultaneously suppressed. Our measurements suggest a route to minimizing dissipation in superconducting devices and provide a benchmark for theoretical efforts aimed at describing the dimensional crossover.

items.title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Bogong moths ( Agrotis infusa ) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps 1,2 . These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the stars as a compass 3 but navigate correctly even when the stars are obscured by clouds 3 , suggesting that their magnetic sense 4 probably harnesses the Earth’s magnetic field as a compass. However, the nature of this compass, and of the magnetic sense underlying it, remains unknown. Here we show that Bogong moths, tethered in a flight arena under a full-spectrum randomized starry night sky, navigate in their inherited migratory direction using the geomagnetic field alone. If the geomagnetic field is turned by 180°, or if inclination is inverted, moths fly in the opposite direction. If polarity is inverted, moths fail to turn. Furthermore, if violet–blue light (380 nm < λ < 500 nm) is removed from the illumination spectrum, or if tethered moths are exposed to weak broadband radiofrequency fields (150 kHz to 60 MHz), magnetic orientation is abolished. Our results indicate that Bogong moths use the geomagnetic field as an inclination compass for long-distance navigation at night and possess a light-dependent radical-pair-based magnetic sense 5 .

items.title: Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE2 production for tumour immune escape
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Ferroptosis, a form of cell death induced by overwhelming membrane lipid peroxidation, is a vulnerability of many cancers, including cancers resistant to current molecular and immune-based therapies 1–7 . Triggering of ferroptosis therefore provides an opportunity to achieve elimination of difficult-to-treat cancers 1–4,8,9 . Studies in mouse cancer models have demonstrated that anticancer immunity, mediated by dendritic cells (DCs) and CD8 + T cells, is essential for effective tumour eradication by ferroptosis-inducing strategies 10–13 . However, ferroptotic cells limit this response 8–10,14 , resulting in immune escape and tumour growth through mechanisms that remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that ferroptotic cancer cells activate a molecular program resulting in aberrant production of prostaglandin E 2 (PGE 2 ), which limits the stimulation of anticancer CD8 + T cell responses by type 1 conventional DCs (cDC1s), thereby promoting immune escape. In ferroptotic cancer cells, lipid peroxidation-mediated membrane permeabilization enables Ca 2+ influx, which activates p38 MAPK signalling and thereby drives PGE 2 production. This signalling axis is uncoupled from cancer cell death and can be targeted to selectively interfere with immune-inhibitory PGE 2 production while preserving ferroptotic cancer cell elimination. In the context of cancer cell ferroptosis, ablation of PGE 2 production or disrupting PGE 2 signalling restores cDC1-mediated anticancer CD8 + T cell responses and leads to effective tumour elimination. Our findings identify a key mechanism that limits antitumour immunity and prevents tumour elimination upon ferroptosis induction in cancer cells, which could be exploited for cancer therapy.

items.title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Large and giant double-stranded DNA viruses substantially affect eukaryotic ecology and evolution 1–4 . They prevail in the environment but are rarely found in the digestive system of animals 5,6 . Here we present the discovery of a diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes, dubbed egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses. Egoviruses are found worldwide, almost exclusively in the digestive system of humans, livestock and wild animals. The most prevalent human-specific egovirus is spread across continents, demonstrating a long-term association between egoviruses and the human gut microbiome. Eukaryotic homologues of egovirus core genes suggest that these viruses primarily infect Trichostomatia (ciliates), which assist ruminant digestive processes 7 , and Parabasalia (Metamonada), which influence animal immunity and gut microbiome ecology 8 . Egoviruses also contributed to the genetic makeup of polintons, endogenous viruses that proliferated in genomes of Trichomonas vaginalis 9 and its close Parabasalia relatives. Unlike poxviruses that form brick-shaped virions, egoviruses are predicted to form multilayered icosahedral capsids resembling those of asfuviruses and probably representing the ancestral virion structure. Egoviruses are the only known clade of double-stranded DNA viruses of eukaryotes prevailing in the animal digestive system. Phylogenomic analysis suggests an evolutionary scenario whereby egovirus-like ancestors of poxviruses infected anaerobic unicellular eukaryotes inside the gut of ancestral animals, before transitioning to animal cell infection, which was accompanied by the virion metamorphosis.

items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The scale evolution of parton distributions is governed by splitting functions. We compute the four-loop splitting functions in perturbative QCD that control the evolution of quark nonsinglet distributions. We confirm previous partial results and obtain, for the first time, fully analytic expressions for all nonsinglet contributions at this order. These allow us to extract the analytic form of the four-loop virtual and rapidity anomalous dimensions entering logarithmic resummation. We provide precise numerical representations of the splitting functions suitable for parton evolution.

items.title: Decreased astrocytic CCL5 by Mir324 ameliorates ischemic stroke injury via the CCR5/ERK/CREB pathway
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Following ischemic stroke, Ccl5 mRNA expression increased, while Mir324 expression decreased in the peri-infarct cortex of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) mice. However, the roles of CCL5 and Mir324 in stroke remained largely unclear. Here, we show that inhibiting CCL5 using antibodies or Mir324 not only reduced infarct area and preserved neurological function in MCAO mice but also attenuated astrocyte reactivity and microglial activation, protected dendritic structures, and maintained spine density. In an astrocyte-neuron co-culture system after oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), inhibiting astrocytic CCL5 by antibody or Mir324 decreased neuronal apoptosis and preserved dendritic structure. Importantly, the suppression of CCL5 enhanced ERK/CREB pathway signaling both in vivo and in vitro. Consistent with these findings, the application of Maraviroc, a CCR5 antagonist, reduced infarct size, decreased neuronal apoptosis, and upregulated the ERK/CREB pathway in neurons treated with OGD. In conclusion, targeting the CCL5 pathway via Mir324 represents a promising therapeutic strategy for alleviating ischemic stroke damage through modulation of the neuronal CCR5/ERK/CREB pathway.

items.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: User simulators offer a scalable way to evaluate interactive agents, but how to assess their quality remains underexplored. In particular, it is unclear whether existing user simulator evaluation frameworks reliably detect meaningful failures in simulated user behavior. This uncertainty makes it difficult to interpret simulator evaluation. To understand what a high benchmark score tells us about simulator quality, we (meta-)evaluate the metrics themselves. To instantiate this meta-evaluation, we deliberately perturb simulated replays to induce failures such as altered goals, omitted constraints, premature stopping, and acceptance of broken work, then test whether the metrics penalize these failures. Evaluation methods from three prior studies detect only 5-6 of the 10 perturbations; their combined scores even favor populations instructed to accept broken work over unmodified controls. Motivated by these gaps, we propose a new evaluation suite that combines utility of user simulators for evaluating agents and two measures of fidelity to real users: population-level fidelity assesses collective interaction patterns, while trace-level fidelity assesses the preservation of individual users' goals, constraints, and persona. Under the same detection criterion, our evaluation suite detects all 10 perturbations. Evaluating six user simulators on 351 real multi-turn sessions in which 348 distinct users across 23 languages and agents work together to create and refine artifacts such as full-stack web apps, games, design assets, and automated workflows, we find that population-level measures can miss when a simulated user pursues the wrong goal, ignores a constraint, or behaves out of character, highlighting the need to assess fidelity at comprehensive granularities.

items.title: Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: A fixed dispatch rate for LLM inference becomes stale as serving fleets resize and request sizes change. Generative output length is unknown at admission, and shared provider pools can lose capacity. We present Cap-and-Track, a design for asynchronous inference across provider capacity and internal GPUs. Meta's traffic shaper implements Cap-and-Track for post and live-video understanding. Refusals signal the backend's current admission ceiling. Durable priority queues hold excess work outside execution, including refused requests for retry. Cap is a fail-fast admission check at the saturated resource that refuses work before a long wait. Using only those refusals, the Track dispatcher probes upward and backs off. It follows the ceiling without output-length prediction or a fleet-level rate to retune. In a concurrent same-traffic production A/B, the shaper ran per-replica Cap plus Track. It served a classifier on 43% fewer H100s than its queued, fixed-rate precursor, though lower-priority work waited longer at backfill peaks. In steady-capacity real-engine replay, Track ran within 1% of the goodput of a fixed rate tuned above measured capacity, with about a quarter of that rate's refusal share. The shaper carries more than 300 million online requests and hundreds of terabytes of media a day. During a backfill, it handled 1.1 billion requests in its busiest 24 hours. Lessons include keeping queues inside inference engines just long enough to fill batches, steering dispatch by capacity refusals alone, keeping dispatch stateful, and sizing fleets by how long low-priority work can wait.

items.title: Measuring and Improving Transfer of Neural Surrogates for Vehicle Aerodynamics
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Neural surrogates for external vehicle aerodynamics are fast alternatives to physics-based computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. Their foundational limitation is a lack of zero-shot generalization across vehicle classes, which results in an expensive, custom training campaign for each new vehicle design. Similar to pretrained models in other fields, a pretrained surrogate should adapt to a new vehicle class using only a few simulations and stay accurate on its pretraining domain. No prior study has systematically tested this transfer behavior. We conduct a large-scale, controlled benchmarking study on five DrivAerML-pretrained surrogates across four independent target datasets. These datasets differ from the source in geometry, CFD solver, turbulence model, and flow conditions. We find that fine-tuning these surrogates outperforms training from scratch in fewer than half of the comparisons and lowers the accuracy of the surrogate on its source dataset. We introduce GeoReplay, a geometry- and gradient-aligned source replay that keeps source simulations resembling the target in training and applies their updates only when they agree with the target gradient. A risk bound separates geometric coverage from differences in the simulated physics, and we prove that every sufficiently small GeoReplay step decreases the target training objective. GeoReplay lowers the source error of fine-tuning in 77 of 80 settings and matches its target accuracy.

items.title: Hardware-Efficient Entanglement Distillation Using Bosonic Systems
items.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated on each paper page)
items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2277 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-11-18-2277 High-fidelity entanglement shared between distant quantum systems is an essential resource for quantum communication and computation. Entanglement distillation addresses this need by converting multiple noisy Bell pairs into fewer higher-fidelity pairs, using only local quantum operations and classical communication. However, this approach typically requires a substantial overhead in the number of qubits. To bypass this hurdle, we propose to leverage the high-dimensional Hilbert space of a $single$ pair of bosonic systems to store a large amount of entanglement, replacing the need for multi-qubit systems. To distill entanglement in such a setup, we devise a new entanglement distillation protocol, tailored for bosonic systems. The protocol converts a highly-entangled noisy state between two bosonic systems into a lower-dimensional but high-fidelity entangled state, using only local bosonic operations. We show that our protocol significantly enhances the fidelity of the entangled state in the presence of naturally occurring loss and dephasing errors. Compared to methods relying on multiple Bell pairs, our scheme offers a more hardware-efficient strategy, providing a practical route toward the realization of entanglement distillation.

items.title: Antiferroelectric hafnia down to the 2D limit
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Antiferroelectricity is a material property characterized by alternating electric dipoles spontaneously ordered in antiparallel directions. Antiferroelectrics are promising for energy storage, solid-state cooling, and memory technologies; however, these materials are scarce, and their scalability remains largely unexplored. In this work, we demonstrated that single-crystalline hafnia, a lead-free complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)–compatible material, exhibits antiferroelectricity under compressive-strain conditions. We observed antiparallel sublattice polarization and stable double hysteresis in single-crystalline (111)-oriented epitaxial lanthanum (La)–doped hafnia films grown on yttrium-stabilized zirconia and showed that the antipolar orthorhombic phase of hafnia adheres to the Kittel model of antiferroelectricity. Compressive strain strengthens the orthorhombic order in thinner La-doped hafnia films, achieving a very high ordering temperature of 850°C in the two-dimensional limit, highlighting hafnia’s potential for advanced antiferroelectric devices.

items.title: An open agentic AI co-scientist for clinical and biomedical discovery
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer’s blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. To support research involving sensitive clinical datasets, OpenScientist can operate in a fully air-gapped environment using open-source models for inference. OpenScientist demonstrates that open, auditable, agentic AI can support real-world clinical research by researching the literature, generating hypotheses, executing analyses, and generating insights from complex datasets.

items.title: Distinguishability of locally diagonal orthogonally invariant quantum states
items.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated on each paper page)
items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2275 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-11-18-2275 We study the distinguishability of quantum states under local operations with classical communication (LOCC), separable, and positive-partial-transpose (PPT) measurements, focusing on locally diagonal orthogonally invariant (LDOI) states – those invariant under local diagonal orthogonal twirling. This class includes many important families such as Werner states, isotropic states, X-states, and Dicke states. We show that optimal PPT and separable measurements for distinguishing LDOI states can always be taken to be LDOI, and the LOCC supremum can be approached by LDOI LOCC POVMs, enabling a dimensional reduction from $n^4$ to $O(n^2)$ in the associated optimization problems. We establish efficiently computable bounds on the distinguishability of orthonormal LDOI bases and prove that for a broad class of such bases – including all two-qubit cases – the LOCC supremum equals the PPT and separable optima. More generally, we show the gap between PPT and LOCC distinguishability is at most $(n-2)/(2n^2)$ for local dimension $n$.

items.title: Polarized positron generation via laser-engineered quasistatic magnetic fields in a spatially extended herringbone target
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Polarized positron sources are of interest for precision studies of spin-dependent interactions and future high-energy colliders, motivating laser-driven approaches for producing relativistic polarized positrons. Here, we propose a scheme in which a herringbone plasma target organizes laser-driven return currents to generate spatially extended quasi-static magnetic fields. Three-dimensional spin-resolved quantum electrodynamics particle-in-cell simulations show that a 3.4-PW laser produces magnetic fields exceeding $10^6$ T, with opposite polarities on the two sides of the target and a duration exceeding 100 fs. A delayed 10-GeV electron beam generates high-energy photons through nonlinear Compton scattering, followed by positron production via the nonlinear Breit--Wheeler process. The resulting positrons exhibit opposite spin polarizations and deflection directions in the two magnetic-field regions, enabling angular selection of positrons with polarization exceeding $63\%$ at a yield of approximately $0.007$ positrons per incident electron, compared with a total yield of $0.029$. More restrictive angular selection can further increase the polarization to nearly $90\%$, albeit at a substantially reduced yield. These results suggest a route to polarized positron generation through the spatial organization of laser-driven quasi-static magnetic fields.

items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Long-read sequencing technologies generate large volumes of data, creating substantial storage and transmission demands. Although reference-based compressors can achieve high compression, their reliance on an appropriate reference genome limits their use. We present LRCBench, a benchmark and survey of reference-free lossless compressors for long-read sequencing data. We review traditional and learning-based general-purpose and sequencing-specific methods, then evaluate 35 compressors on 16 real-world datasets from Oxford Nanopore and PacBio platforms. We compare compression ratio, storage savings, runtime, peak memory use, and robustness across datasets. Learning-based compressors are evaluated on six MinION datasets because of their high computational costs. CoLoRd achieves the best overall compression ratios in our experiments, while other methods offer trade-offs in speed, memory use, and robustness. We also examine multithreaded speedup and discuss future directions in parallel acceleration, privacy protection, adaptive parameter tuning, and hardware-algorithm co-design.

items.abstract: We investigate quasicoherent modes (QCMs) and their interaction with scrape-off-layer (SOL) plasma blobs (filaments) in the type-I-ELM-free quasicontinuous exhaust (QCE) regime, extending the analysis in [K. Zhang et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 055102 (2026)]. Two-fluid electromagnetic turbulence simulations are compared for two self-consistent turbulence states with different separatrix densities. In both cases, a separatrix-spanning QCM resides within the radial-electric-field well, whereas blobs are observed only in the case with higher separatrix density. The QCM exhibits similar kinetic-ballooning-mode (KBM) signatures in both cases, with modest differences in coherence and harmonic content. The primary difference is the presence of an additional resistive X-point mode (RXM), which emerges as the near-X-point collisionality increases. The coexistence of the KBM and RXM shifts the potential--density cross-phase from its KBM-like value toward the interchange value in the SOL, allowing QCM perturbations to be ejected as blobs. These intermittent blobs account for over half of the net radial $E\times B$ transport in the far SOL. Neither QCM onset nor blob ejection requires an increase in upstream collisionality. The results distinguish the KBM-dominated mechanism that regulates the pedestal from the RXM-assisted blob-launching mechanism that enables intermittent SOL exhaust.

items.title: Effect of scrape-off losses and current flattening on runaway electron dynamics in ARC
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Disruptions in high-current tokamaks, such as ARC, may result in megaampere-scale runaway electron currents. In this work, we evaluate mitigation strategies via massive material injection, accounting for the combined impact of scrape-off losses due to vertical displacement events and current profile relaxation during the thermal quench. We find that scrape-off losses alone yield only modest reductions in runaway electron currents, but combining them with current flattening creates a beneficial synergistic effect. The latter broadens the current channel outward, shifting efficient runaway electron generation closer to the plasma edge where the dynamically contracting boundary can effectively scrape off the electron beams. This interplay significantly expands the operational window for mitigation toward lower assimilated densities, theoretically reducing runaway currents to manageable levels at experimentally feasible assimilated quantities.

items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: {Magnetic-field control and synchronization are essential requirements in laboratory plasma experiments investigating wave propagation and plasma instabilities. In this work, an Embedded Trigger Control System (ETCS) has been designed and implemented for synchronized operation of a pulsed Helmholtz coil system and a broadband whistler-wave exciter in the Large Volume Plasma Device--Upgrade (LVPD-U). The experimental configuration employs an electrostatically shielded loop antenna driven by a thyratron-switched pulse-forming network to launch broadband whistler waves in the frequency range of approximately 150~kHz to 5~MHz. Simultaneously, a pulsed Helmholtz coil capable of generating magnetic fields up to $\pm150$~G is used to modify the local magnetic topology and create transient magnetic-null configurations. The developed ETCS utilizes the controlled evolution of the Helmholtz circuit $L/R$ time constant through the introduction of a lumped series inductor, enabling precise magnetic-field ramping and dynamic timing control. A microcontroller-based trigger architecture determines the desired firing instant from the calibrated current evolution of the Helmholtz circuit and synchronizes wave excitation with a prescribed magnetic-field amplitude. The system extends the effective circuit time constant by more than an order of magnitude, allowing accurate and repeatable wave launching during controlled magnetic-field evolution. The implemented approach provides a simple, reliable, and versatile synchronization platform for wave--plasma interaction studies requiring precise temporal coordination between pulsed magnetic-field generation and wave excitation.

items.title: Cross-species digital xenocortication model delineates molecular correlates of human brain connectome
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Cross-species digital xenocortication (CSDX) model based on pairing of a human brain structure with one or more mouse brain structures was constructed and implemented to dissect the molecular correlates of the human brain connectome. Design of the CSDX model is based on the assumption that a human brain region and its named mouse counterpart occupy corresponding positions in an evolutionary conserved mammalian brain connectome plan, so that a projection strength measured between two mouse structures is informative about the relation between the two human structures paired with them. In the CSDX model, gene expression for the node was measured in the human brain, while connection strength between two nodes was measured in the mouse brain. CSDX models of different parcellations were employed to explore the potential regulatory associations of brain connectome patterns and constituents of protein-protein interaction (PPI) cascades of hybrid assembly pathways of endogenous multiprotein complexes. Metrics of continuous engagement of the PPI cascade nucleated protein dimers of CORUM multiprotein complexes have been identified as statistical components of the multivariate transcriptome-connectome associations. It accounts for additional connectome associated variations beyond the five measured axes in the 82 nodes CSDX model. Comparisons of the seven arm models of transcriptome-connectome associations demonstrate that the mouse derived model generally fits the mouse brain connectome better, while the human derived model assigns a significantly larger fraction of its transcriptome-connectome association to unique rather than net shared contributions. This study nominates elite panels of top scoring candidate protein dimers and CORUM multiprotein complexes for follow up mechanistic studies of their potential roles in structural functional features governing mammalian brain connectome.

items.title: Dynamic functional connectivity reveals evolving neural activity states of alcohol-seeking in rats
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Yujing Zhang, Nicholas M. Timme, Mintao Liu, Christopher C. Lapish, Joaquín Goñi The brain mechanisms underlying persistent alcohol-seeking in Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) remain incompletely understood. To investigate this behavior, we characterized the temporal evolution of neural activity states in the anterior cingulate cortex of freely behaving rats performing an aversion-resistant drinking (ARD) task. Alcohol-preferring (P) rats were assessed, as they reliably exhibit ARD when alcohol is devalued with the bitter tastant quinine. P rats were compared with Wistar rats, which progress slower to ARD, as indicated by cessation of drinking following quinine devaluation. Using dynamic functional connectivity analyses of spike-train recordings, we identified latent neural states corresponding to seeking and non-seeking phases. We then integrated the latent-state decoding of neural activity with a seeking intensity model derived from the observed drinking behavior. items.abstract: Eukaryotic initiation factor 4E (eIF4E) drives cap-dependent translation, regulated by 4E-binding proteins (4E-BPs) competing for its dorsal and lateral surfaces. CYFIP1, a scaffold protein, is both a WAVE Regulatory Complex component and a non-canonical 4E-BP repressing translation via a short helical motif, linked to autism spectrum disorders and cancer. Prior work modeled only this isolated motif as a peptide, leaving the full interface uncharacterized. Starting from this preliminary evidence, we modeled the full-length proteins as flexible partners: all-atom simulations fed a data-driven docking search (HADDOCK3), which guided funnel-restrained Temperature-Accelerated Molecular Dynamics of a coarse-grained Martini 3 representation. Ten replicas accumulated 100 $μ$s of enhanced sampling. Funnel-restraint variables efficiently sample binding and unbinding but are structurally degenerate: direct clustering of the raw trajectory collapses these poses into poorly resolved groups. We instead reweighted the biased trajectories onto a contact-based latent space built by benchmarking PCA against a beta-Variational Autoencoder, then clustered minima of the equilibrium free-energy surface: only intermediate regularization resolved distinct, homogeneous modes. Three such modes recur, engaging eIF4E's canonical dorsal site, its non-canonical lateral site, and both. We find that CYFIP1 also engages eIF4E through a second surface, the same that mediates its WAVE-complex dimerization, and a basic patch. Both plausibly explain residual binding previously reported after motif mutation. This suggests its translational and cytoskeletal roles compete for the same surface. Most contacts on eIF4E fall outside this dorsal/lateral interface. This heterogeneous, plastic ensemble offers a structural basis for mutagenesis and therapeutic peptide design.

items.abstract: by Artoghrul Alishbayli, Karol Przewrocki, Paul van Heumen, Bernhard Englitz Sound detection amidst noise presents an important challenge in audition. Many naturally occurring sounds (rain, wind) can be described and predicted only statistically, so-called sound textures. Previous research has demonstrated the human ability to leverage this statistical predictability for sound recognition, but the neural mechanisms remain elusive. We trained mice to detect vocalizations embedded in sound textures with different statistical predictability, while recording and optogenetically modulating the neural activity in the auditory cortex. Mice showed improved performance and neural encoding if they could sample the statistics longer per trial. In summary, mice exploit stimulus statistics to improve sound detection in naturalistic background noise, reflected in behavioral performance and neural activity, relying on PV interneurons for temporal integration.

Existing G × G association methods are restricted to either single or multiple continuous phenotypes. Here we introduce GiMat (Gene Interaction and Multiple-phenotype Association Test), a statistical framework that extends multivariate kernel regression to model G × G interactions jointly across dichotomous phenotypes, while explicitly capturing homogeneous and heterogeneous interaction effects. items.abstract: by Siyu Liang, Ziyi Wang Forward Head Posture (FHP) is a prevalent postural abnormality among adolescents, linked to musculoskeletal imbalances and long-term health risks. To investigate its prevalence and develop a research-stage screening framework, we conducted a large-scale population study involving 1,577 Chinese adolescents, recruited for the screening and assessment of FHP. Building on this cohort, we propose an end-to-end predictive framework that integrates human pose estimation with tabular machine learning. RTMPose was used to extract key anatomical landmarks from side-view images, followed by the computational derivation of seven predefined, anatomy-informed posture features. A TabPFN classifier trained on these features achieved an F1 score of 82.46% and an AUC of 0.837. Permutation-based SHAP analysis identified the horizontal angle between the right eye and shoulder as the strongest predictive contributor. A SHAP dependence plot also suggested a potential nonlinear dependence between features beyond that captured by pairwise correlation. These associations describe the behavior of the fitted model and do not establish causal biomechanical effects. These findings support the feasibility of a non-invasive and interpretable image-based framework for FHP screening. items.title: Micrograph B-factor estimation via Wilson statistics
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The single-particle cryo-electron microscopy imaging process is known to cause exponential decay in the amplitude and power spectra of proteins. This decay is modeled by the B factor and is currently corrected as a post-processing stage of the 3D reconstruction. As a consequence, all experimental images in the dataset are assumed to share the same B factor. In this paper, we suggest a novel approach wherein the B factor is determined and corrected as a preprocessing step to the reconstruction. We show such an approach can improve reconstruction resolution.

items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Telomere shortening is a hallmark of aging, yet telomere length (TL) varies considerably between individuals and is strongly influenced by inheritance. In mice, efficient mitochondrial function and low reactive oxygen species (ROS) production are essential for telomere elongation during early embryogenesis. As mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) encodes several subunits of the electron transport chain, we investigated whether mtDNA variants influence TL using a transmitochondrial cybrid model.
